text:
anya: FYI I ran into a confusing DX hole while following the "edge quickstart" sample — types behave in node dev but vanish after the edge bundle step.

matt: can you show the small repro? is this the same thing where generic overloads collapse to `unknown`/`any`?

anya: minimal: we wrap the SDK call with a retry helper typed as overloads: `function withRetry<T>(fn: ()=>Promise<T>): Promise<T>; function withRetry(fn){...}`. In TS build for node-local it keeps `T`, but once the sample is bundled for the edge runtime the call sites infer `unknown`.

ravi: likely a declaration resolution problem between the SDK's conditional exports and the bundler's type rewriting. Which bundler?

anya: Vite + rollup for edge bundle. package.json has exports pointing to `./dist/esm/index.js` and `./dist/cjs/index.cjs`, and types map to `./dist/types/index.d.ts`. Edge build seems to pick a flattened single d.ts that uses `export =` fallback.

zoe: note: TS overloads + generic inference are brittle when the compiler can't see a clear single signature. If the declaration file ends up with an `export =` wrapper, inference can be lost.

anya: quick repro at call site: `const user = await withRetry(()=> sdk.getUser<{id:string}>(id))` -> in edge bundle `user` is `any`.

andre: workaround: avoid overloads for retry wrapper; use one generic signature: `function withRetry<T>(fn: ()=>Promise<T>, opts?: RetryOptions): Promise<T>` — eliminates ambiguity.

matt: short term fixes for sample: 1) pin tsconfig moduleResolution to `node` (not `bundler`) for the sample build so dts remain stable; 2) ensure `types` in package exports points to ESM types explicitly; 3) add `skipLibCheck: true` during bundling step to avoid dts flattening.

ravi: longer term: SDK maintainers should consider consolidating declaration shapes (avoid dual `export =` + ESM `export` combos) or provide a small `types/edge.d.ts` entry for edge builds.

zoe: also saw auth wrapper problems: when we had `wrapAuth` as an overloaded function to support callback vs promise styles TS lost contextual return types in edge builds, causing folks to cast to `any` and hide the issue.

anya: that was exactly the onboarding pain — new users copy sample, sprinkle `as any`, and ship.

pkg-bot: CI summary: node-cjs typecheck OK. edge-bundle typecheck: failures in 3 tests referencing `withRetry` inference.

andre: Proposed actions: A) update sample README with a short section "Edge bundlers & TS caveats" listing `moduleResolution`/`module`/`type` settings; B) add a sample-level CI job that runs real bundler + `tsc` to catch rewrites; C) change retry/auth helpers in SDK to single generic signatures or discriminated unions where overloads are necessary.

matt: also add a lint rule for samples forbidding `as any` and `// @ts-ignore` (with a short comment allowed in prod tests).

ravi: can someone open a small reproducible issue + PR with the sample config tweaks? I'll help wire up the CI job.

anya: opened issue #4128 and drafted a PR with tsconfig change + CI workflow. PR link in the issue. Also added a tiny note in onboarding docs about prefer explicit generic assertions when using edge bundles.

zoe: thanks. this will save a lot of confused fast-path users.

an y a: noted typo: "anya" signing off.
